source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Work on Attention Layer Outputs

record.tranche_reason: The post uses sparse autoencoders as a tool for interpreting attention-layer activations and investigating circuits. Its reported interpretability results concern SAE features, not the neuron poles or neuron explanations named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports an interpretability estimate for SAE features in the first 50 features and a dead-feature rate for the SAE. These are related to interpretability but do not measure neuron poles or neuron-level explanation accuracy. The cited Anthropic SAE results are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The post trains a sparse autoencoder on attention-layer z vectors of a two-layer model and interprets its SAE features. It does not audit neuron poles, score neuron explanations, or build neuron-level attribution graphs. Its interpretability shares are for SAE features, a different unit from the neurons the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAEs on attention outputs learn sparse, interpretable features, and that upstream and downstream circuits can be traced from them. They also find induction feature families (~5% of living features) and evidence of attention-head polysemanticity. They acknowledge polysemanticity at low activations, suboptimal proxies and SAE training that could be improved.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains an SAE on concatenated attention-head z vectors from a two-layer model and interprets its features. It does not use the neuron-explanation audit or held-out activation-scoring procedure described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that feature activations are more specific to their proposed contexts at higher activation ranges and more polysemantic at lower ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow inspection of the first 50 attention-output SAE features in gelu-2l: 76% are alive, and 82% of the alive ones are judged interpretable. About 24% of all SAE features are dead.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features on attention outputs of a small model are mostly interpretable by shallow inspection.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep dives show feature activations are highly specific to the proposed context at high activations but polysemantic at low activations. Pearson correlation between the 'board' feature and its proxy is 0.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For SAE features, an explanation from top activations predicts high-activation firing but not low-activation firing. This is analogous to V6, but the unit is an SAE feature, not a neuron.

record.problems: The authors describe the shallow feature investigations as potentially misleading, say the SAE may be too small, and report that their proxies are suboptimal. Their interpretability estimate is based on only the first 50 features and is not a neuron-level audit.
record.rows_left_out: No direct neuron-level results are reported. Detailed case-study results and induction-family analyses concern individual SAE features or attention heads, not neuron poles or neuron explanation accuracy.
